newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bovespa sees no capital outflows on CPMF tax woes.
newsitem.headline: Bovespa sees no capital outflows on CPMF tax woes.

text.p: The Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) said it has not registered any capital outflows ahead of the so-called CPMF check tax on financial transactions which will take effect next year.
"So far we haven't noticed any outflow because of the CPMF," said Bovespa president Alfredo Rizkallah.
The CPMF check tax will levy 0.2 percent on all financial transactions and is aimed at funding health services.
So far this month net foreign capital inflows into the Sao Paulo bourse have totalled 172.8 million reais. Between January and November, net foreign capital inflows amounted to 2.7 billion reais.
Rizkallah said he expects the government to exempt foreign investors in the stock market from the CPMF tax.
"I believe we can reach a solution regarding foreign investors soon," he said.
Rizkallah said the government could exempt stock trade from the CPMF tax by reducing the 0.2 percent tariff to zero for foreign investors, "without altering the legislation."
The Bovespa chief noted Brazil should give foreign investors the same conditions they have overseas to invest.
"They can be here or in Indonesia," he said.
Rizkallah praised today's approval by the Chamber of Deputies of a new corporate law which he said would facilitate Brazil's key privatizations.
He also said the bourse's average turnover has risen 36.7 percent so far this year, when compared with the same period of 1995. So far market average turnover was $387 million.
